questions.question: Does ATS software automatically reject resumes that don't match keywords?
questions.answer_summary: A 2025 study surveying 25 US recruiters found 92% said their systems do not auto-reject based on formatting, design, keywords, or AI match scores; only 8% use auto-rejection, and only for highly specialized roles.

questions.question: What percentage of resumes never reach a human recruiter?
questions.answer_summary: The widely-cited '75% of resumes get rejected by ATS' figure has been debunked by recent recruiter-survey research; the study traced the stat's origin mainly to job-seeker social media posts (68%) and career-coach marketing (20%), not verified data.

questions.question: What do ATS platforms like Greenhouse, Lever, and Workday actually do with a resume?
questions.answer_summary: They use NLP-based parsing to convert resumes into searchable, structured data, support recruiter Boolean/keyword search, and apply recruiter-defined 'knockout questions' (e.g., licensure, work authorization) — they don't independently rank or reject candidates.

questions.question: Do hidden white-text keywords actually trick ATS into ranking a resume higher?
questions.answer_summary: Coverage from recruiters described these 'hidden prompt' tricks as generally ineffective and risky if discovered during manual review.
sources: https://news.google.com (Built In: 'AI Resume Hacks? Recruiters Say Hidden Prompts Don't Work,' Oct 2025)

questions.question: Are newer AI hiring tools introducing bias risks beyond old-style keyword matching?
questions.answer_summary: BBC reported that AI-driven hiring tools may be filtering out qualified applicants due to pattern-matching flaws, a distinct and newer risk from classic ATS keyword filtering.
sources: https://news.google.com (BBC: 'AI hiring tools may be filtering out the best job applicants,' Feb 2024)

questions.question: What resume qualities do recruiters actually prioritize when they manually review applications?
questions.answer_summary: Per the 25-recruiter study: clear/scannable structure (92%), relevant experience and skills (88%), tailored content matching the job (76%), and short achievement-focused bullets (72%).

questions.question: Does complex resume formatting (tables, columns, graphics) actually break ATS parsing?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — this is described as a real (not mythical) mechanism: NLP-based parsers can misread multi-column layouts, tables, and embedded graphics, corrupting the extracted text.

questions.question: Why do some candidates get hired despite an 'unoptimized' resume?
questions.answer_summary: A Business Insider piece profiled a candidate who ignored standard ATS-tailoring advice and still got hired, suggesting human review, referrals, and overall fit often outweigh keyword-perfect formatting.
sources: https://news.google.com (Business Insider: 'My bad resume still got me hired,' Jul 2025)

questions.question: Do different ATS vendors behave differently enough that a single 'ATS trick' can't work universally?
questions.answer_summary: Market share is fragmented (Greenhouse ~19%, Lever ~17%, Workday ~16%, iCIMS ~15%), meaning tailoring advice aimed at one vendor's quirks doesn't reliably transfer to another.
sources: https://ongig.com (via Jobscan/Ongig research on ATS market share)

questions.question: Is there credible research on hiring processes systematically excluding qualified candidates?
questions.answer_summary: Harvard Business School's 'Hidden Workers: Untapped Talent' research specifically studied how efficiency-focused hiring technology and processes exclude categories of otherwise-qualified workers (caregivers, veterans, people with disabilities, etc.).

questions.question: Are developers now building tools specifically to test or beat ATS parsing?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — Hacker News Show HN launches include an open-source 'ATS-style resume simulator' and AI agents built specifically to tailor resumes against ATS/job-description matching.

questions.question: What's the actual scale of ATS adoption among employers?
questions.answer_summary: Roughly 98.4% of Fortune 500 companies (492 of 500) and about 35% of small businesses now use some form of ATS.
